home.name: Hero search bar rebuild (trip type + combobox + time)
home.why: The hero currently collects occasion, a flat <select> of every pickup point, date and package — but not the two inputs that move the price most: trip type and pickup time. tripType lives only in the calculator, so a visitor who lands wanting a Kochi to Munnar drop is routed into a local-package browse page and the driver-return allowance appears as a surprise later. Every competitor (Blacklane, Discover Cars, Gozo, Clear Car Rental, Tejas) puts trip type above the fields and time beside the date.
home.spec: See the `searchBar` field for the full spec. Files: components/home/HomeSearch.tsx, components/home/HomeSearch.module.css. Reuse components/ui/LocationCombobox.tsx (already built for the calculator) instead of the flat select. No new data: locations already carry citySlug/isAirport, packages already carry label, and the trip options come from the same list as components/calculator/Calculator.tsx so the two screens cannot drift.

home.name: How a booking actually works — four steps, money included
home.why: There is no checkout, so the page has to replace one. Every Indian operator ships a 3-step 'enquire, confirm, travel' block and every one of them stops before the money, which is exactly the unanswered question for someone about to hand a stranger their wedding morning. Naming the advance %, what document backs it, and when the balance is due is the cheapest removal of hesitation on the site, and both numbers are already in settings.
home.spec: Heading: kicker 'How it works' / h2 'From this page to a confirmed car'. New components/home/HowItWorks.tsx + .module.css, inserted in app/page.tsx between the pricingBand section (~line 150) and the 'Why Xotic' section (~line 190). Four cells in the existing `grid-4`, white background (the page already carries three black bands, this one must read as plain fact). Each cell: a large thin numeral (48px, weight 200, ink at 18% opacity) top-left, an 18px title, a two-line 14px body. Hairline connectors between cells on desktop only. Copy, with {advancePercent} and {gstPercent} interpolated from catalog.settings so it can never drift from the engine: (1) 'Price it here' — 'Pick the car and the package and see the full itemised price. No form, no login, no account.' (2) 'Send it on WhatsApp' — 'The message carries the breakdown, so we are both looking at the same numbers.' (3) 'Pay {advancePercent}% to hold the date' — 'Against a GST invoice. No payment happens inside WhatsApp.' (4) 'Balance after the trip' — 'Itemised the same way, with extra km and hours at the rates you already saw.' Under steps 3 and 4 add a 12px muted artefact line: 'GST {gstPercent}% invoice' and 'Final bill, same line items'. DATA: settings.advancePercent and settings.gstPercent, already editable at /admin/settings. Store the four {title, body} pairs as a new `how_it_works` JSON column on site_settings following the existing why_items pattern so the owner can correct wording without a deploy; fall back to the copy above when empty.

home.name: What can and cannot change your price (shared ChargesExplained band)
home.why: Bata, night charge and the one-way return allowance are precisely the charges Indian customers have been burned by, and not one competitor explains them — they either hide behind 'all-inclusive' (Gozo) or list terse T&C lines (GetMeCab's 'Driver allowance INR 200 to INR 400'). Xotic's engine already computes each as a named QuoteLine, so the explainer costs zero new data and is the highest-leverage differentiator available. Built once, it earns its keep on four pages.
home.spec: Heading: kicker 'No surprises' / h2 'Nothing appears on your bill that is not on this page'. New shared component components/trust/ChargesExplained.tsx with props { car?, settings, variant: 'band' | 'plain' }. On the home page render the 'band' variant (black, `on-dark`) replacing the current pricingBand blurb text, keeping the live preview quote card beside it. Six short cards in a 3x2 grid, each a title plus two sentences; where a car is passed, interpolate its real numbers, otherwise state the rule without a figure: (1) 'Driver bata — his food and stay. Charged per calendar day of the trip, not per hour.' (2) 'Night charge — applies only when your PICKUP falls between 10pm and 6am. A 9pm pickup that runs past midnight does not attract it.' (3) 'One-way drops — the chauffeur has to bring the car home empty, so we charge 35% of the distance back at the extra-km rate, not a second full package.' (4) 'Extra km — past the km your package includes. The estimate is on the quote before you send it.' (5) 'Extra hours — billed to the half hour past the package allowance.' (6) 'Tolls, parking and state permits — at actuals on the day, with receipts. They are not in the quote because they depend on your exact route.' Close with one line: 'GST at {settings.gstPercent}% applies to the total. There is nothing else.' DATA: every rule is already implemented in lib/pricing.ts (ONE_WAY_RETURN_SHARE = 0.35, NIGHT_START_HOUR/NIGHT_END_HOUR, bata x days); per-car figures from the Car record; gstPercent from settings. Reuse on app/price-calculator, app/cars/[slug] and app/cities/[slug] — identical text on four pages is the point, because a policy that reads the same everywhere reads as a policy rather than a pitch.

home.name: Rewrite the 'Why Xotic' grid as chauffeur standards
home.why: The chauffeur IS the product and the risk — a stranger drives your family, and at a wedding he is in the photographs. Savaari, Tejas and every credible operator lead with vetting because it is the one real differentiator against a rideshare. Xotic's grid-5 already exists and is already admin-editable; it is currently generic 'why us' copy doing a weaker job than it could.
home.spec: Heading: kicker 'The person who drives you' / h2 'What every Xotic chauffeur is held to'. No new component — rewrite the five settings.whyItems entries at /admin/settings and keep the existing grid-5 in app/page.tsx (~line 190), which already renders {icon, title, body}. The five items must be operational commitments the owner can actually keep: police-verified and background-checked; in uniform for weddings and VIP movement on request; trained on your city's routes rather than following a phone blindly; his name, phone number and the car's registration sent to you on WhatsApp before pickup; the same chauffeur for the whole booking, he does not change mid-trip. Add one small markup addition below the grid — a second sub-list, 'and what he will never do': take a second booking on your day, ask you for cash, smoke in the car. The negative half is the more persuasive half and nobody writes it. DATA: settings.whyItems, already a JSON array editable in admin, so this is mostly a content change. CONSTRAINT: the pre-pickup handover line ships only if the owner confirms it actually happens; if it does, append the matching sentence to the outgoing message template in lib/quote.ts so the promise is visibly kept.

browse.name: All-in price on the car card, with a 'Price details' disclosure
browse.why: Two cards can only be compared if both numbers mean the same thing. CarCard currently prints carPrice() as the headline and then a strip of '+₹X/km after' and 'Driver bata ₹Y/day' — two charges in the price's neighbourhood but not in the price, so the visitor has to do arithmetic to compare and is primed to expect more charges they have not been shown. Turo rebuilt its listings specifically to collapse itemisation into one trip price with the detail on demand.
browse.spec: Files: components/CarCard.tsx, components/CarCard.module.css. Headline becomes the all-in figure for the selected package: rateFor(car, pkg.rateKey) x city.multiplier + car.bata, plus GST at settings.gstPercent — labelled '{price} all-in' with a 13px second line 'includes chauffeur, fuel, bata and {gstPercent}% GST · {pkg.label}'. Replace the rates strip with a single ghost 'Price details' control expanding a native <details> in place: package base, city multiplier x{multiplier}, driver bata, GST, then a muted tail 'Extra km ₹{extraKmRate}/km · Extra hour ₹{extraHrRate}/hr · Night pickup ₹{nightCharge}'. CRITICAL: add an exported helper `allInFor(car, city, pkg, settings)` to lib/pricing.ts and have the card, the car-detail booking panel and CarStickyBar all read from it — three surfaces must never print different numbers. Update the browse lede to match: 'Prices include chauffeur, fuel, bata and GST for the {pkg.label} package in each car's home city.' DATA: entirely existing — Car rates, City.multiplier, settings.gstPercent.

browse.name: Sticky results bar: count, applied-filter chips, sort
browse.why: app/cars/page.tsx already renders a resultsHead with a count and a 3-option segmented sort, but it scrolls away. Deep in a filtered list the visitor loses track of why the list looks the way it does, and the only way to undo one filter is to scroll back to the rail. Baymard's product-list research is explicit that active filters need an overview separate from the filter interface, each individually removable.
browse.spec: File: app/cars/page.tsx plus a small CSS module. Restructure resultsHead into two lines and make it sticky: `position: sticky; top: var(--header-height); z-index: 20;` with the page background and a 1px bottom hairline so it reads as a rule, not a floating card. Line 1: '{cars.length} cars' left, the existing `.seg` sort control right — keep the segmented control, at three or four options it shows the choices without a click. Line 2: one chip per non-default value in the parsed CarFilters (city, type, occasion, seats — parseFilters in lib/catalog.ts), each labelled with the human label ('Kochi', 'Luxury sedan', 'Wedding', '5-7 seats') and a trailing x linking to the same URL minus that one param, plus a ghost 'Clear all' reusing the existing clearHref. Line 2 renders nothing when no filter is applied, so an unfiltered page keeps its calm. DATA: existing filter parsing, no schema change. NOTE: do NOT add a 'Top rated' sort — see the rejected list on ratings.

browse.name: Mobile filter sheet with the live count in the Apply button
browse.why: components/browse/FilterSidebar.tsx is a server component of link-chips that below 1023px simply stacks under the grid, so on a phone the visitor scrolls past a wall of filters to reach a single car. Every comparable site collapses to a sheet, and putting the result count inside the commit button is the cheapest possible preview — you learn a combination is empty before you apply it and have to back out.
browse.spec: Split components/browse/FilterSidebar.tsx: keep today's markup as the desktop rail (>=1024px), and add a client wrapper that below 1024px renders a 'Filters' button into the sticky results bar, badged with the number of non-default values in CarFilters. Tapping it mounts the same groups inside a <dialog> bottom sheet — translateY(100%) to 0, backdrop, focus trap, Esc and backdrop-tap close. Inside the sheet, selections are LOCAL state rather than immediate navigation, so the footer can run the same predicate as filterCars() over catalog.cars client-side and label the primary button 'Show {n} cars' (disabled, 'No cars match', at zero). Fixed footer: 'Clear all' ghost left, primary right. Apply pushes the composed URL. Sort stays in the bar, not in the sheet — sort and filter are different decisions and merging them costs a tap on the more common one. DATA: catalog.cars serialised to the client wrapper; filterCars() is already pure and importable.

browse.name: Fleet comparison table view
browse.why: Card grids are good for browsing and bad for choosing. Once a visitor has narrowed to three or four cars they want them side by side, and a table is the only honest way to show that bata and extra-km rate differ per car — which is where the real cost difference between a Camry and a Fortuner actually lives. Tejas's 14-row 'Complete Fleet Comparison Table' is the most-copied section in the category for exactly this reason.
browse.spec: Heading: 'Compare the fleet'. Add a 'Cards / Table' toggle beside the sort segment, driven by a URL param `view=table` so it is shareable and server-rendered. Table rows: Car (thumbnail + name + year) | Type | Seats | 8 hrs / 80 km | 12 hrs / 120 km | 24 hrs / 300 km | Extra km | Extra hr | Bata. Package prices = rateFor(car, rateKey) x the selected city's multiplier, driven by the city selector already in the sidebar; extra km/hr and bata come straight off the Car record and are NOT multiplied — say so in the caption: 'Package prices for {city.name}, before GST. Extra km, extra hours and bata are the same in every city.' Wrap in overflow-x:auto; below 768px force the card view regardless of the param. Car names link to /cars/{slug}. DATA: all existing.

carDetail.name: Stop showing admin placeholder copy to customers
carDetail.why: components/ui/Media.tsx renders the caller-supplied placeholder string as visible text, and every public caller passes admin-facing copy — app/cars/[slug]/page.tsx passes `Drop ${car.name} photo` and CarCard passes the same. Any car with an empty images array is currently telling a customer 'Drop Fortuner photo'. On a premium product that reads as an abandoned listing. It is the highest-value small fix in the whole set.
carDetail.spec: Two parts. (1) Media gains `variant?: 'public' | 'admin'`, defaulting to 'public'. 'public' ignores the placeholder string and renders a large type-appropriate Phosphor icon (ph-car-profile, ph-van for MUV, ph-car-simple for sedan) at 25% opacity on var(--color-neutral-900) at the frame's aspect ratio, with a 12px caption 'Photo on request'. 'admin' keeps today's 'Drop … photo' copy and is passed only from app/admin/fleet/*. Keep the four fixed thumbnail slots rendering so the layout is identical with and without photos. (2) On app/cars/[slug]/page.tsx, when car.images.length === 0, add one line under the gallery: 'Photos of this exact car on WhatsApp. The car supplied is this model or an equivalent of the same class.' — the 'or similar' convention Blacklane uses, which also forecloses the complaint at handover. DATA: none.

carDetail.name: Remove the star rating and the aggregateRating schema
carDetail.why: Car.rating is rendered as '4.9' with a star glyph in CarCard (line ~82) and emitted from components/seo/JsonLd.tsx (line 74) as an aggregateRating with ratingCount: 1. There is no reviews platform behind it. A buyer sophisticated enough to be choosing a wedding car knows a self-hosted 4.9 with no review count and no source is decorative — and once one element is spotted as decorative, the itemised price loses credibility by association. The schema emission is worse than merely dishonest: unbacked AggregateRating risks a structured-data penalty and consumer-protection exposure.
carDetail.spec: (1) components/CarCard.tsx line ~82: delete the rating block. If `rating` is genuinely an internal fleet-condition grade, relabel it as one ('Fleet grade A') and explain the scale — never a star glyph. (2) components/seo/JsonLd.tsx lines 74-79: delete the aggregateRating object entirely; keep the rest of CarJsonLd (name, brand, offers with the real package price), because Product/Offer markup is legitimate and useful. (3) app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx lines 72 and 156 and components/cards/CityCard.tsx: City.carCount is commented in lib/types.ts as a marketing headline, not live inventory, but the city hero currently reads '{carCount} cars on call across {city}', which implies availability. Rephrase to a national claim if true, or replace with a count that IS live — cars whose homeCitySlug matches. (4) Add `google_reviews_url` to site_settings and, only when set, render a plain outbound 'Read our Google reviews' link in the footer: a link the visitor can verify beats a quote they cannot. DATA: removal only, plus one optional settings column.

carDetail.name: Extend the rate card into a full 'what this car costs' table with a city switcher
carDetail.why: The rate card exists but prices only the car's home city, and it sits below the specs rather than acting as the page's answer block. Tejas's Rolls-Royce Ghost page — the richest template in the competitive set — runs exactly this table directly under the gallery, with every number the customer will later be billed for in one place. It pre-empts the three charges Indian customers distrust by naming them as line items rather than letting them appear on WhatsApp.
carDetail.spec: File: app/cars/[slug]/page.tsx, extending the existing rateRows table. Add above it a city chip row — 'Rates shown for {city.name}' — with a client-side select over catalog.cities that swaps the multiplier live (a small client island wrapping the table only, so the page stays a server component). Rows: the three packages from catalog.packages, each labelled '{pkg.label} — {pkg.sub}' at rateFor(car, pkg.rateKey) x city.multiplier; 'Extra km' ₹{extraKmRate}/km; 'Extra hour' ₹{extraHrRate}/hr; 'Driver bata' ₹{bata}/day, note 'his food and stay, per calendar day'; 'Night charge' ₹{nightCharge}, note 'pickup between 10pm and 6am'; 'Seats / transmission / fuel'; 'Fuel and chauffeur' → 'Included in every rate'; 'Tolls, parking, state permits' → 'At actuals on the day'; 'GST' → '{gstPercent}% on the total'. Orange accent on the three package rows only. Show the pre-GST figure with GST as a separate visible row — the category convention is '₹7,400 plus GST', and a single all-in number reads as suspicious to this market. Move the whole block directly under the gallery, above the specs, then render <ChargesExplained car={car} variant='plain' /> below it. Also rewrite the luggage spec card from the current seat-count ternary into the alternatives form chauffeur sites use — sedan '2 check-in or 4 cabin bags', SUV '3 check-in or 5 cabin', MUV '4 check-in or 6 cabin' — since luggage, not seats, is what decides an airport or wedding-party booking. DATA: all existing.

carDetail.name: Booking panel and sticky bar quote one live all-in figure
carDetail.why: components/car/CarBookingPanel.tsx and CarStickyBar already react to PackageSelectionProvider, so the structure exists — what is missing is the number. The visitor is comparing a car against a budget, not against a rate card, and keeping a live total in view as they change package is what converts browsing into an enquiry. The two surfaces must never be allowed to print different numbers.
carDetail.spec: In the panel, under the package selector: a two-line live estimate — big figure = allInFor(car, city, pkg, settings), the shared helper introduced in the browse spec; small line 'all-in for {pkg.label} in {city.name} · before extra km'. Below it a collapsed 'See the breakdown' <details> rendering the existing components/quote/QuoteLines.tsx against a default local trip, so the same itemised component the calculator and booking summary use appears here too. Reorder the CTAs: 'Build the exact quote' (btn-solid, carrying the existing calculatorParams) FIRST, WhatsApp second — the calculator produces a far better WhatsApp message than a cold enquiry. Foot of the panel, 13px muted: '{advancePercent}% advance · No online payment · GST invoice on request'. CarStickyBar mirrors the identical figure and identical primary CTA from the same helper. DATA: existing.

carDetail.name: 'See the exact message you'll send' preview bubble
carDetail.why: A wa.me link is an opaque door: the visitor does not know whether tapping it sends something instantly, what it says about them, or whether they will look foolish. Showing the payload converts an unknown action into a reviewed one — the job an order-review step does before checkout. It doubles as pricing proof, because the itemised message IS the quote, so the number on screen is visibly the number they will be held to. Almost nobody in the category ships this.
carDetail.spec: New components/quote/MessagePreview.tsx taking the `message` string already returned by resolveQuote() in lib/quote.ts — zero new data. Native <details>/<summary> labelled 'See the exact message you'll send', open by default on desktop, collapsed on mobile so it costs no layout. Bubble: max-width 520px, background #f6f6f4, 3px left border in #d17200, radius 10px, 13px/1.6, white-space: pre-wrap so the message's newlines survive. Caption under it: 'Nothing is sent until you press the button inside WhatsApp.' Add a 'Copy message' secondary button beside the WhatsApp CTA for desktop users on WhatsApp Web. Render on app/booking-summary above SendToWhatsApp, in components/calculator/Calculator.tsx under the total, and on car detail against carEnquiryMessage(car, city, pkg) — a one-line bubble there, still worth showing.

carDetail.name: FAQ accordion, generated from catalog data
carDetail.why: It is the last objection-clearing surface before the enquiry, and on a WhatsApp funnel every question answered here is a message round-trip the operator does not have to run. Every competitor closes with 6-9 of them and they answer a remarkably consistent set. Generate rather than hand-write so the answers cannot go stale against the engine. Caveat: FAQ rich results were removed from Google Search in May 2026 — build this for readers, keep the markup, expect nothing from the SERP.
carDetail.spec: New components/content/FaqBlock.tsx taking `items: {q, a}[]`, rendered as native <details> so the text is in the HTML rather than JS-gated, plus an FAQPage emission added to components/seo/JsonLd.tsx. Author the generators once in lib/content.ts so /cities/[slug] and /occasions/[slug] can render their own variants. Car-page questions, all answered from live data: 'What does the {car.name} cost for a day in {city.name}?' (quotes the three package prices); 'Is this self-drive?' ('No. Every Xotic booking is chauffeur-driven. Fuel and the chauffeur are in the rate.'); 'What is driver bata and why is it separate?' (₹{bata}/day, his food and stay); 'Do you charge extra for a night pickup?' (₹{nightCharge}, pickups between 10pm and 6am only); 'What happens if I go past {pkg.km} km?' (₹{extraKmRate}/km, shown on the final bill); 'Are tolls and parking included?' (from settings.exclusions); 'How much advance do you need?' ({advancePercent}%, no online payment); 'Can you supply more than one car for a wedding convoy?'. Keep to eight — Gozo's twenty-plus reads machine-generated, the opposite of Xotic's register. DATA: all derivable.

city.name: Priced hero with a breadcrumb
city.why: The searcher arrives from 'car rental with driver in Kochi' with two questions: do you cover my city, and roughly what does it cost. The current hero answers neither — it says '350 cars on call', a marketing count, and forfeits the one claim this page is uniquely able to make. Gozo leads with 'starting at Rs 12.5/km'; Avis leads with a rate card. The number in the first screen is also the line Google and AI answer surfaces quote back.
city.spec: Keep the black hero band and the city photo. Replace the blurb with three computed facts: (1) 'From ₹{min over cars where homeCitySlug === city.slug of rateFor(car, "rate_8h") x city.multiplier, inc. GST} for 8 hrs / 80 km with a chauffeur'; (2) '{cars based here} cars · {count of locations with citySlug === city.slug} pickup points · {airport location name}'; (3) H1 becomes 'Chauffeur-driven car rental in {city.name}' with the state as subhead — the current H1 is just the city name, a wasted heading. Two CTAs: 'Price a route in {city.name}' to /price-calculator?city={slug}, and the WhatsApp button. Add a breadcrumb strip above the hero (Home / Cities / {city.name}); it is currently missing and it is the anchor for BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, the one schema type that still reliably changes the SERP line. DATA: all existing. Drop or rephrase the carCount stat per the rating-and-counts fix in carDetail.

city.name: Route fare table, framed as a published price list
city.why: This is the load-bearing section on every competitor city page and the highest-intent organic entry point in the category — people search the route, not the brand. cityRouteFares() already yields name/km/packageLabel/price, but it prices only the cheapest local car and the rows are not actionable. A business that publishes numbers reads as one that will not invent them on the phone.
city.spec: Heading: kicker 'Published fares' / h2 'Fares from {city.name}'. Upgrade cityRouteFares() in lib/catalog.ts three ways. (a) Add a car dimension — three 'from' columns: cheapest sedan, cheapest SUV/MUV, and the top luxury car based in the city, so the table shows a range the way Gozo's does. Columns: Route | Distance | About {km / 45 km/h, rounded to the half hour} | Sedan from | SUV from | Luxury from. (b) Make every row actionable: the route cell links to /price-calculator?city={city}&from={fromSlug}&to={toSlug}&pkg={packageSlug}&trip=oneway so the calculator opens pre-filled, and a trailing cell carries a WhatsApp link naming that exact route and price. (c) A framing line above the table sourced from settings rather than hard-coded: 'One-way drop, car based in {city.name}, chauffeur, fuel, bata and {gstPercent}% GST included. Tolls, parking and airport entry at actuals.' Close with one CTA: 'Not your route? Price your own.' DATA: catalog.cityRoutes (admin-editable at /admin/routes), lib/distance.ts (kmOverride, else haversine x circuityFactor), lib/pricing.ts. GAP TO CLOSE FIRST: this needs 5+ routes per city in the admin to read as a price list rather than a sample.

city.name: 'What a car costs in {city}' — the package rate sheet
city.why: The route table answers 'what does my trip cost'; the rate sheet answers 'what are your rates' — a different query and a different buyer (corporate, wedding planner, repeat customer). Publishing extra-km and extra-hour rates pre-empts the biggest objection in chauffeur rental, fear of the bill growing after the trip. It also replaces the current thin 'rate notes' card, which states the multiplier without ever showing what it does to a number.
city.spec: Heading: 'What a car costs in {city.name}'. Table over cars where homeCitySlug === city.slug: Car (linked to /cars/{slug}) | Seats | 8 hrs / 80 km | 12 hrs / 120 km | 24 hrs / 300 km | Extra km | Extra hr | Driver bata. Package prices = rateFor(car, pkg.rateKey) x city.multiplier; extra km/hr and bata are NOT multiplied and the caption must say so. GST stated as a footnote, not folded in. Directly below, a short 'how this price is built' list in the calculator's own vocabulary: package base x the {city.name} multiplier of x{city.multiplier}, extra km, extra hours, driver bata, night charge for 10pm-6am pickups, one-way return allowance, occasion surcharge, {gstPercent}% GST. Then the existing CarCard grid. Place immediately after the route table. DATA: all existing.

city.name: Airport pickups in {city}
city.why: Airport pickup is the highest-frequency, lowest-deliberation chauffeur job and its query volume dwarfs everything else on a city page ('COK airport taxi', 'cab from Kempegowda airport'). It also carries the most anxiety — delayed flight, nobody at arrivals — so it converts on reassurance rather than price. A city page without it forfeits the largest keyword cluster it could own, and the data (isAirport on LocationPoint) is already there.
city.spec: Heading: 'Airport pickups in {city.name}'. Render only when catalog.locations contains a row with citySlug === city.slug && isAirport. Two columns. Left: the named airport plus a mini fare table of airport to the two or three most-asked drop points, reusing cityRoutes rows that touch the airport or computing via cityRouteKm(). Right: reassurance lines, but ONLY ones that are derivable or that the owner confirms in writing. Safe: 'One-way drops carry a driver-return allowance — 35% of the distance at ₹{extraKmRate}/km, shown on your quote'; 'Airport entry and parking are at actuals'; 'Pickups between 10pm and 6am carry a night charge of ₹{nightCharge}'; 'Send your flight number on WhatsApp and it stays with the booking'. Do NOT ship flight tracking, a meet-and-greet name board or a free-wait window unless the owner states the real policy — those are operational promises, not data, and an unkept one at 2am is the worst possible first impression. CTA: WhatsApp pre-filled 'Airport pickup in {city.name} — flight number, date, time'. DATA: locations (admin-editable at /admin/locations), cityRoutes, Car record.

city.name: City x occasion strip
city.why: City x service is where the commercial long tail lives — 'wedding car rental in Kochi' converts far harder than 'car rental Kochi'. The cross-links also spread authority from the city page, which earns links, to the occasion pages, which earn money, and tell Google the two are one topical cluster rather than two orphans. The link graph must run both ways.
city.spec: Heading: 'What people book us for in {city.name}'. Four cards in grid-4, one per catalog.occasions entry: occasion.icon, the name scoped to the city ('Weddings in Kochi', 'VIP and celebrity movement in Kochi', 'Casual city use', 'Outstation tours from Kochi'), occasion.tagline, and a from-price computed as the cheapest car in carsForOccasion() intersected with homeCitySlug === city.slug, on the 8hr/80km package x multiplier. Where occasion.surcharge > 0, state it on the card honestly — '+₹{surcharge} handling: {occasion.handlingNote}' — rather than letting it surface for the first time in the quote. Links to /occasions/{slug}?city={citySlug}. Reciprocally, add an 'Available in' city row to each occasion page linking back. DATA: catalog.occasions (admin-editable at /admin/occasions), carsForOccasion() in lib/catalog.ts.

city.name: City FAQ accordion
city.why: Same component as the car-page FAQ, different generator. On-page it kills the objections that otherwise become a WhatsApp back-and-forth or a lost enquiry; off-page it is now the main way a page gets quoted in AI answer surfaces. Eight questions with real numbers beat Gozo's twenty padded ones and match Xotic's calm register.
city.spec: Reuse components/content/FaqBlock.tsx with a city generator in lib/content.ts. Eight questions, answers interpolated from live data so they cannot go stale: 'What does a car with driver cost in {city.name}?' (the real 8/80 from-price and the x{multiplier} rule); 'What is driver bata?'; 'Is there a night charge?' (10pm-6am, ₹{nightCharge}); 'What happens on a one-way drop?' (the 35% return allowance, explained); 'Are tolls and parking included?' (settings.exclusions); 'How do I pay?' ({advancePercent}% advance, no online payment, balance after the trip — state it plainly, the absence of an online checkout is a trust asset here, not a liability); 'Which airport do you cover?'; 'Can I keep the same chauffeur across a multi-day trip?'. Emit FAQPage JSON-LD alongside. Place second to last, above the cross-links. DATA: derivable; a `city_faqs` override table would be nice later but is not needed to ship.

city.name: 'Where people go from {city}' — distance and drive-time cards
city.why: Distance and drive time are the two facts a customer needs to judge whether a day trip is even feasible, and answering them reinforces the fare table's credibility. This is the honest substitute for the tourism-prose filler that makes competitor city pages look mass-produced — Clear Car Rental opens with two paragraphs on Bangalore as 'Silicon Valley of India', exactly the thin content every service-area SEO guide warns against.
city.spec: Heading: 'Where people go from {city.name}'. Four to six cards built from catalog.cityRoutes: destination name, km (cityRouteKm), realistic drive time phrased 'about 5 and a half hrs' (km / 45 km/h, rounded to the half hour), which package fits ('needs the 24 hr / 300 km day'), and one sentence of operational advice in Xotic's voice ('leave by 6am or you lose an hour on the ghat road'). Each links into the pre-filled calculator. Plus one authored paragraph per city — two to four sentences on how chauffeur days actually run there (traffic windows, wedding-season pressure, temple dress codes, airport entry rules) — stored in a new nullable `intro` text column on the cities table with a textarea added to /admin/cities. Render nothing when empty. Two honest sentences beat six paragraphs of generated copy. DATA: cityRoutes plus one new admin field.

cityIndex.name: A coverage comparison table, not a tile wall
cityIndex.why: The index has two jobs: convince a visitor whose city may or may not be covered, and act as the crawl hub pushing all six city pages into the index. A grid of three tiles and one line of copy does the first slowly and the second weakly. Nobody in the competitive set does this page well — Blacklane ships a bare alphabetical list, Clear Car Rental a 40-name footer dump — which is exactly why doing it well is cheap advantage.
cityIndex.spec: File: app/cities/page.tsx. Heading: h1 'Six cities, one fleet, one price list'. Below the lede, a scannable table, one row per city: City (linked) | State | Rate multiplier | Cars based here | 8 hrs / 80 km from | Airport served | Most-asked route. Every column is computed from the existing catalog — City.multiplier, cars filtered on homeCitySlug, min rateFor(car, 'rate_8h') x multiplier inc. GST, the isAirport location for that city, and the first cityRoutes row. Caption: 'The multiplier is the city's operating cost applied to the package base. Extra km, extra hours and bata are the same everywhere.' Keep the existing CityCard grid below the table for warmth — the table is the payload, the cards are the texture. DATA: all existing.

cityIndex.name: The full route index
cityIndex.why: Every published route across all six cities in one list turns this page from a signpost into a real destination for 'X to Y cab fare' searches, and it links deep into all six city pages, which is how the city pages get crawled at all. It costs one map over data that already exists.
cityIndex.spec: Heading: 'Every route we publish a fare for'. A three-column list (single column on mobile) over the whole of catalog.cityRoutes, grouped by city with the city name as a subheading: '{from} to {to} · {km} km · from ₹X'. Each entry links to /price-calculator pre-filled with from/to/city/trip=oneway. Add ItemList JSON-LD over the routes so the published fares are machine-readable to AI answer engines. DATA: catalog.cityRoutes + lib/distance.ts + lib/pricing.ts, no new fields. This is the section that most rewards the owner adding more routes in /admin/routes.

cityIndex.name: 'What you get in every city' and 'Not on this list?'
cityIndex.why: Stating the inclusions once here means the six city pages do not have to repeat them and go duplicate against each other. And a visitor from Coimbatore or Goa currently bounces off a six-tile grid with no answer — outstation runs reach anywhere from these six bases, and saying so honestly converts a bounce into a WhatsApp message.
cityIndex.spec: Two short blocks under the table. (1) 'What you get in every city' — settings.inclusions as a check list beside settings.exclusions as an 'at actuals, with receipts' list, closing with 'GST at {gstPercent}% on the total, {advancePercent}% advance to hold a date, no online payment.' Use the same three-column In-the-price / Not-included / At-actuals treatment as elsewhere so it reads as one policy. Note that /admin/settings already labels exclusions as 'Paid at actuals', so split any genuinely never-included item out of that list rather than inventing a new column. (2) 'Not on this list?' — 'Outstation runs reach anywhere in India from these six bases. Tell us the route and we will price it.' with a WhatsApp CTA and a link to the calculator, whose place index already covers 2,948 Indian places, so this is a promise the product can actually keep. Add BreadcrumbList and ItemList JSON-LD for the six cities. DATA: settings only.

cityIndex.name: Coverage map
cityIndex.why: A map answers 'do you cover me' faster than any table, and components/map plus lib/map.ts already exist for the calculator, so the marginal cost is low. It is warmth rather than payload, which is why it ranks below the table.
cityIndex.spec: Above the table: one map with six city pins from City.lat/lng plus the served locations from catalog.locations, each pin linking to its city page. No routing lines, no animation — a static, calm plot in the site's own palette, orange pins on a desaturated base. Height capped around 380px, full width, no interaction beyond the pin links so it never traps a mobile scroll. DATA: City.lat/lng and LocationPoint.lat/lng, both already stored and admin-editable.

searchBar:
Keep the existing card shape and the occasion tab row at the top, and add exactly two things — a trip-type row and a time field. Final field order:

Row 0 — Occasion tabs (unchanged): Wedding / Celebrity / Casual / Outstation, from catalog.occasions.

Row 1 — NEW trip-type segmented control, three options, reusing the `.seg` / `.seg-opt` classes /cars already uses and sourced from the same trip-options constant as components/calculator/Calculator.tsx so the two screens can never drift: 'In the city' (local, sub-label 'Car stays with you') / 'One-way drop' (oneway, 'Driver returns empty') / 'Round trip' (round, 'Out and back'). Default local.

Row 2 — Pickup location: replace the flat `<select id="home-from">` with the existing components/ui/LocationCombobox.tsx. Typeahead over catalog.locations with grouped results — 'Airports' first (isAirport, ph-airplane-takeoff), then one group per city in catalog.cities order (ph-map-pin), each row showing the location name with the city name as dim secondary text. Cap at 8 visible rows. Keep the 'Use my current location' button, but on success set the input's visible text to the matched location's name, not just the state, so the visitor sees what was chosen.

Row 2b — Drop-off location: appears only when trip type is oneway or round, immediately under Pickup, same combobox but backed by the full 2,948-place index via /api/places so an outstation destination is reachable.

Row 3 — Pickup date and Pickup time side by side at 1fr each. Time is a select in 30-minute steps from 00:00 to 23:30, default 10:00 — never free text. The instant a 22:00-05:59 time is chosen, show a 13px inline note under it in var(--color-accent) with ph-moon: 'Night pickup — a night charge applies.' lib/pricing.ts already treats 22:00-05:59 as the night window, so this is live logic, not copy. Disclosing the night charge in the hero rather than at the quote is the whole trust play; the amount itself stays on the car.

Row 4 — Package select, full width. When trip type is oneway or round, replace it with a read-only note: 'Priced on distance — the 24 hr / 300 km day applies.'

Submit: 'See cars and prices', carrying pkg, from, to, date, time, city (derived from the pickup point), occasion AND trip into the /cars URL. Extend tripDefaults() in lib/catalog.ts to read `trip` and `time` so /price-calculator opens on the right trip type instead of resetting to local.

Mobile: the segmented control wraps to full width with the sub-labels dropped; date and time stay side by side because they are the pair people fill together; everything else stacks. No modal, no multi-step — the card must stay one screen tall on a phone.

Why this and not the alternatives: trip type is the single fork that changes the fare structure, so it has to be resolved before anything else is asked; time is the second-biggest mover and is currently collected nowhere in the hero; and a grouped typeahead beats a flat select of 30+ unfamiliar point names, especially on a phone where a long native select is a full-screen wheel. Nothing here needs data the site does not already hold, and the combobox component already exists.

rejected.name: Testimonial wall / review carousel (Luxorides, Gozo pattern)
rejected.reason: There is no review platform, no collected quotes and no permission to name customers. Every one would have to be written by us. Fabricated social proof on a site whose entire funnel is a WhatsApp handshake is both the worst trust risk available and a consumer-protection exposure. The honest substitutes are already in the plan: published fares, an itemised quote, and a message preview.

rejected.name: Star ratings and AggregateRating schema
rejected.reason: Car.rating is an unsourced number with no review count behind it, and components/seo/JsonLd.tsx currently emits it as aggregateRating with ratingCount: 1. Not merely uncorroborated — unbacked AggregateRating markup risks a structured-data penalty. Specced for REMOVAL in the carDetail list rather than extension. Do not add a 'Top rated' sort on /cars for the same reason.

rejected.name: 'X,000 weddings served' / 'trusted by N customers' counters
rejected.reason: No booking count exists in the data model; the enquiries table records enquiries, not completed trips. Any figure would be invented. City.carCount cannot stand in either — lib/types.ts explicitly comments it as a marketing headline, not live inventory.

rejected.name: Driver profile cards with photos, names and per-driver ratings (Savaari, Gozo)
rejected.reason: There is no drivers table, no photos and no ratings. Savaari can do this because it has a driver database and post-trip ratings; Xotic has neither. With a shared roster across a small fleet, profiles would be fabricated or permanently stale, and a stale profile is worse than none. Replaced by the chauffeur-standards rewrite of settings.whyItems, which is an operational commitment rather than a fake identity.

rejected.name: 'Avg reply 8 min' or any stated response-time badge
rejected.reason: Nothing measures reply time. It is a promise the site cannot keep at 2am, and the first broken one destroys more trust than the badge ever built. Ship it only if the owner supplies a window he will actually honour, stored in a new site_settings column and rendered only when set.

rejected.name: Live availability, 'only 2 left for your date', countdown timers, 'N people are viewing this'
rejected.reason: Twice disqualified: there is no availability data of any kind, and manufactured scarcity is against the brief's calm editorial register. The FTC also treats misleading availability claims as deceptive. The honest version of urgency — an owner-authored wedding-season lead-time table — is listed separately below.

rejected.name: Six-row graded cancellation table and refund-timeline table (Tejas pattern)
rejected.reason: Not a data problem but a policy problem: no cancellation terms exist to publish. Invented percentages would be worse than silence because customers would hold the business to them. If the owner writes a real policy it belongs beside advancePercent in site_settings as three rows at most — Xotic takes no online payment, so the six-row version answers a question nobody asked.

rejected.name: Wedding peak-season booking lead-time table
rejected.reason: Requires operational knowledge the data does not hold: how far ahead the flagship cars actually get blocked in December. It is the strongest booking trigger on Tejas's wedding page and worth building LATER as an owner-authored JSON field on the occasions table, but it is not derivable, so it is not in this plan.

rejected.name: Per-city chauffeur counts, years-driving and languages-spoken block
rejected.reason: Real data the business holds offline, but not in the schema and not in admin. It would have to be typed as prose per city with no validation and would go stale silently. Fold the true, universal parts into settings.whyItems instead, where one edit updates every page.

rejected.name: Flight tracking, meet-and-greet name board and free-wait-window promises in the airport block
rejected.reason: Copied straight from Gozo and Avis, these are operational commitments rather than facts about the fleet, and the airport section converts precisely because such promises are believed. An unkept one at 2am is the worst possible first impression. The airport block ships with derivable content only, plus whatever the owner confirms in writing.

rejected.name: Supplier/company filter and pay-now vs pay-later toggle on /cars
rejected.reason: Both imported from multi-supplier aggregators (Discover Cars, Hertz). Xotic is a single supplier with no online payment; either control would advertise a choice that does not exist.

rejected.name: Driver-age and country-of-residence fields in the hero (Discover Cars)
rejected.reason: Meaningless when the driver is Xotic's. Adding fields to a hero form is expensive; adding ones that cannot affect the price is pure friction.

rejected.name: Converting headline pricing to '₹X/km'
rejected.reason: The category convention, but the package model (8hr/80km bundles) is the clearer and more premium framing and it is what the engine computes. Per-km belongs only inside the outstation explanation, never as the headline. Recorded here so nobody re-litigates it.

rejected.name: Twenty-plus FAQs per page and sixty-row fare tables (Gozo)
rejected.reason: Reads as machine-generated, the exact opposite of the brief's dense-but-calm register. Eight FAQs with real numbers, and only the routes actually run, beat volume — and volume is what makes competitor pages look mass-produced.

notes:
BUILD ORDER. Three things should land before any new section, because none of them is a feature and all three are liabilities: (1) export `allInFor(car, city, pkg, settings)` from lib/pricing.ts — the browse card, the car-detail booking panel and CarStickyBar must be incapable of printing different numbers, and today there is no shared helper; (2) the Media `variant` fix, a ten-minute change that currently shows "Drop Fortuner photo" to customers on any car with an empty images array; (3) delete the aggregateRating block at components/seo/JsonLd.tsx lines 74-79.

THREE COMPONENTS, TEN PLACEMENTS. Repetition is the category norm, not a flaw — booking steps, charge explanations and the fleet table recur verbatim on every deep page of the strong competitors. Build ChargesExplained, FaqBlock and MessagePreview once each and place them across home, /cars/[slug], /cities/[slug], /occasions/[slug], /price-calculator and /booking-summary. Identical text on six pages reads as a policy; six variations read as marketing.

OCCASION PAGES (the requested schema has no slot for them, so recorded here). Two changes deserve the same priority as the 'must' rows above. First, restructure occasion.packages[] on the wedding page around ROLE rather than car class — 'Bridal or groom arrival', 'VIP family and elders', 'Guest movement between venues' — each listing two or three real cars from car.occasions with their live 8hr/80km price for the selected city. Wedding buyers shop by job-to-be-done, not by car. Second, add a `timeline` JSON array of {when, what} to the occasions table, rendered as a vertical hairline timeline: 'T-3 hrs — car reaches the decorator, we send you a photo before it leaves', 'T-90 min — at your gate', 'through the photo session — chauffeur waits with the AC running'. This is the honest replacement for testimonials: an itinerary demonstrates you have run this exact day many times, where a testimonial merely asserts someone was happy, and it needs no customer's permission and no invented names. Content must be authored by the owner from how the business actually runs; render nothing when the array is empty.

DATA GAPS, RANKED BY WHAT THEY UNBLOCK. (a) cityRoutes needs 5+ rows per city — without them the route fare table, the city-index route list and the drive-time cards are all thin, and it is the single highest-value hour the owner can spend in /admin/routes. (b) locations needs at least the airport, the main railway station and two or three landmark pickups per city, or the airport block and the grouped combobox have nothing to group. (c) Car images: every empty array is now a calm 'Photo on request' tile rather than an error, but photographs are still what sells a wedding car. (d) Optional new columns, in payoff order: cities.intro (text), site_settings.how_it_works (JSON), site_settings.google_reviews_url (text), occasions.timeline (JSON). Everything else in this plan is derivable from what already exists.

ONE THING THE COMPETITION GETS WRONG AND XOTIC SHOULD KEEP GETTING RIGHT. Show prices pre-GST with tax as a separate visible line, the way the category does ("₹7,400 plus GST"). A single all-in figure reads as suspicious to this market even when it is the more honest number. The one exception is the browse card, where two cars can only be compared if both figures mean the same thing — there, quote the all-in and put the split one tap away in the disclosure.

WHAT NOT TO EXPECT FROM THE FAQ MARKUP. FAQ rich results were restricted in 2023 and removed from Google Search in May 2026. Ship FAQPage JSON-LD because it is cheap and machine readers still parse it, but budget no SERP gain against it. The schema effort that still pays is BreadcrumbList (currently missing on city pages), Service with areaServed and hasOfferCatalog on city pages, and ItemList over the published route fares — entity and price markup, which is what AI answer surfaces actually read.

CONFIDENCE NOTE ON THE RESEARCH. Sixt, Enterprise, Savaari, CabBazar and WTI Cabs all returned 403s or JS shells, so patterns attributed to them come from search summaries and help-centre pages rather than first-hand DOM reads. Everything in the 'must' rows above is corroborated by at least one page that was actually fetched (tejastravels.com, gozocabs.com, clearcarrental.com, avis.co.in, blacklane.com, discovercars.com, kayak.com/cars) or is a fix to code in this repo that I read directly.
